proof_summary: Factoring Wilson’s congruence for the next prime gives \(p_k!\,\prod_{j=p_k+1}^{p_{k+1}-2}j\equiv1\pmod{p_{k+1}}\); parity makes every gap at least two, and gap two is exactly the twin-prime case, where the intervening product is empty, while otherwise this identity yields the stated equivalence. A finite prime-counting sieve identifies the primes at indices 991 and 992 as 7841 and 7853, and direct modular computation shows that their intervening product is \(1\bmod 7853\).
